paragraphs: IKE Smart City builds interactive digital kiosks for city streets, with touchscreens aimed at people on foot. The kiosk programme is delivered at no cost to the cities that host it.

The screens carry listings of restaurants, shops, activities, services, and resources. Those listings are geo-located and updated in real time, and inclusion is free for area businesses. Wayfinding shows real-time transit information, route schedules, mapping, and directions. Each unit also works as a free WiFi hotspot meant to improve access to social services. Other applications list area shelters and point to addiction recovery, food assistance, and job listings.

IKE launched in Denver, with the goal of a wayfinding and city communication system delivered on a self-sustaining business model. Networks have since spread to urban cities nationwide. Design, engineering, manufacturing, permitting, construction management, content management, maintenance, and media sales are all handled in house.

quote.text: Each kiosk offers a hyper-local experience designed to drive discovery, mobility, and equity across the economic spectrum.
